page: Amazon Web Services m6i.32xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 128 vCPUs, consisting of 64 physical cores and 2 threads per core, running at a speed of 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in CPU-intensive tasks, with the Passmark CPU score, extended instructions, and encryption tests all ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is also highly capable, reaching 333.99 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores falling in the middle 50%.

The server demonstrates a clear tradeoff in specialized workloads. While it achieves strong results in static web serving throughput at 70.73 GB/sec and prompt processing for small to medium language models, text generation for large 70B models is weak, falling into the bottom 25% at 2.75 tokens/sec due to the lack of GPU acceleration. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for resource-dense, multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, such as database operations, web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale enterprise applications, but is less suited for single-threaded tasks or large-scale AI model text generation.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.32xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 128 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, paired with 512 GB of DDR4 memory. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this server provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 50 Gbps network interface. Benchmarks indicate top-tier CPU performance, particularly in multi-core operations, encryption, and database tasks, placing it in the top 10% to 25% of tested systems. Conversely, single-core metrics are average, and large-scale LLM text generation is weak due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. This configuration is highly suited for multi-threaded enterprise applications, database operations, and high-throughput web serving, offering strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for balanced, non-GPU workloads.
